Continuation completed for the only selected chapter, 1B. No score was assigned.

The workspace remained read-only, so I could not persist changes to `research-ledger-manifest.json`. Proposed manifest additions are included below.

### New evidence units

- **E026 — ERPA radioactive-source security awareness, 23 June 2022.** An Ethiopian Radiation Protection Authority representative presented target-year work on stakeholder awareness, safety/security of radioactive sources, and resilience during unplanned situations. This establishes institutional activity and cooperation, not effective safeguards or Abiy-specific direction. Lenses: `1B.1, 1B.6, 1B.7, 1B.8`. [IAEA conference record](https://conferences.iaea.org/event/262/contributions/21327/)

- **E027 — EPHI–APHL biosafety partnership, 15 September 2022.** EPHI and the Association of Public Health Laboratories discussed laboratory leadership, equipment maintenance, quality systems, biosafety, biosecurity, and external-quality assessment. This supports target-year institutional capacity-building with federal attribution, but not personal attribution to Abiy or proof of implementation quality. Lenses: `1B.3, 1B.6, 1B.7, 1B.8`. [EPHI announcement](https://ephi.gov.et/the-ethiopian-public-health-institute-and-the-association-of-public-health-laboratories-usa-vow-to-further-strengthen-their-partnership-and-collaborations/)

- **E028 — Reported cyberattack mitigation, 14 February 2022.** INSA reported more than 3,400 attempted attacks over six months, including attacks against government, financial, health, education, regional, and media institutions, and claimed 96% mitigation capacity. This is a contemporaneous official/agency claim relayed by ENA; it lacks independent verification and should be read alongside Freedom House’s contrary evidence and disputed attack-count reporting. Lenses: `1B.5, 1B.7, 1B.9, 1B.10`. [ENA report](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/en_33455)

- **E029 — 2022 biosafety and biosecurity guidelines.** Search validation confirmed that EPHI’s second-edition guidelines were dated September 2022. The PDF gateway returned an access/interstitial page, so no page-level content could be independently validated. Disposition: `discovery_only`, `underlying_source_missing`; do not count as final evidence. [EPHI PDF](https://ephi.gov.et/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Biosafety-and-Biosecurity-Guidlines-for-Health-Laboratories-in-Ethiopia-Second-Edition-1.pdf)

### Rejected or bounded contrary searches

- **E030 — OPCW chemical-incident hospital training, March 2022.** Rejected for Ethiopia-specific evidence: the OPCW lists participants from Burundi, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, and Rwanda, not Ethiopia. [OPCW record](https://www.opcw.org/media-centre/news/2022/03/hospitals-east-african-community-increase-preparedness-chemical-incident)

- **Nuclear safeguards status.** The current IAEA country page identifies Ethiopia as non-party to the CPPNM Amendment and records its Additional Protocol signature, but the page is current rather than a historical 2022 snapshot. Retain only as `context/discovery_only`, not target-year evidence. [IAEA country record](https://ola.iaea.org/Applications/FactSheets/Country/Detail?code=ET)

- **Contrary cyber search.** Freedom House documents government cyberattack exposure, disputed attack figures, and concerns about surveillance and institutional independence. This remains contrary/context evidence rather than proof of either effective defense or harmful cyber conduct. [Freedom House 2022](https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-net/2022)
